stance: Focused course problem-solution essay based on assigned readings, not an exhaustive literature review.
scope: University students: separation from home, disrupted class relationships, academic pressure and uncertainty about future careers; maintaining familiar relationships, developing hobbies, and volunteering or internships.
external_search: None: assigned full texts and reference metadata supplied locally.

sources.file: Assignment_Guidelines_export/2. Reducing Loneliness on College Campuses_Psych Today.pdf
sources.locator: pp. 1–2: distinction between social isolation and loneliness; fitting in versus belonging
sources.role: Definition and relationship quality; expert commentary rather than an intervention trial.

sources.file: Assignment_Guidelines_export/5. Addressing loneliness amongst university students.pdf
sources.role: Systematic review: transition pressures, reported mental health associations, social connectedness interventions, stigma and uncertain lasting effects.

claim_map.claim: Unmet needs for connection and belonging, beyond physical isolation.
University transition involves academic and social pressures; the paragraph now progresses through context, question, solution and conclusion.
claim_map.limit: Class stability and career uncertainty remain qualified student interpretations.

claim_map.claim: Social connectedness interventions show promise; magnitude of benefits unclear.
claim_map.limit: Calls to family and hobby examples are student proposals; the paper is not claimed to have tested those exact activities.

claim_map.claim: Interventions promoting social interaction show promise in reducing student loneliness.
claim_map.limit: Volunteering and internships are introduced as applications of the general principle, not interventions specifically tested by this review. Career exploration and skill development remain conditional student suggestions.

screening.reason: Global public health scope exceeds the chosen student-belonging focus.
Directly discusses university belonging and relationship quality.
Technology and living alone do not directly address the chosen campus programme.
Shared lunches are an illustrative activity, without importing meal-sharing health claims.
Provides full-text synthesis of university loneliness interventions and their limitations.

contrary_or_limits: Uncertain benefit magnitude is retained in paragraph 3. The review also finds uncertain persistence; no lasting cure is claimed. Excessive practical commitments may add pressure.
citation_delta: Added an in-text Ellard et al. (2023) citation to paragraph 4 with an explicit evidence-to-application transition. No bibliography entries added or removed.
student_input: User reasoning supplied on 20 October 2026 governs all three responses and the argument about changing classmates and career uncertainty. No personal experience was invented.
